title: Astrome Secures Rs 64 Crore RDI Funding to Build AI-Powered Satellite Network
summary: Astrome secures 64 crore RDI funding to build AI satellite network
detailed: Bengaluru-based Astrome Technologies has secured Rs 64.05 crore from the Technology Development Board (TDB) under the Department of Science and Technology (DST) through the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund to develop an indigenous artificial intelligence-powered electronic intelligence (AI-ELINT) satellite constellation.
The project will integrate an electronic intelligence (ELINT) payload, AI-based ground processing software and inter-satellite communication links.

sentences: Bengaluru-based Astrome Technologies has secured Rs 64.05 crore from the Technology Development Board (TDB) under the Department of Science and Technology (DST) through the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund to develop an indigenous artificial intelligence-powered electronic intelligence (AI-ELINT) satellite constellation.
The project carries an estimated investment of Rs 128.11 crore, with TDB structuring its financial assistance as optionally convertible debt.
The initiative aims to strengthen India's domestic capabilities in satellite-based signal intelligence and strategic space technologies.
The TDB funding will support the development and deployment of approximately 50-kg microsatellites in low Earth orbit (LEO).
The project will integrate an electronic intelligence (ELINT) payload, AI-based ground processing software and inter-satellite communication links.
The payload will detect and analyze signals across a broad frequency spectrum, while the ground-based software will process the collected intelligence.
Inter-satellite links will enable communication between spacecraft, supporting coordinated data exchange across the constellation.
The network also aims to expand geographical coverage and increase the frequency of observations over identified areas of interest as additional satellites enter orbit.
The funding agreement does not disclose any equity allotment, investor ownership or shareholding changes, as the assistance is structured as optionally convertible debt.
Founded in 2015 by Neha Satak and Prasad H.
Bhat, Astrome Technologies is a deep-tech company incubated at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru.
The company develops wireless and satellite communication products using millimeter-wave and phased-array technologies.
Its portfolio includes patented flat-panel antennas, software-defined modems, beamsteering algorithms and E-band wireless radios designed to deliver high-speed broadband connectivity.

Through solutions such as GigaMesh and its satellite communication systems, Astrome serves telecom operators, enterprises, satellite operators, defense establishments and infrastructure providers.
Its business spans terrestrial wireless connectivity and satellite-based communication across low, medium and geostationary Earth orbits.
The latest project extends its technology development into electronic intelligence and strengthens its positioning in India's strategic space technology ecosystem.
The project aims to advance its underlying technologies from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-4 to TRL-9 through engineering, system integration, testing and validation.
This progression will take the technology from laboratory-level validation to a fully demonstrated operational system.
TDB Secretary Rajesh Kumar Pathak said the RDI Fund supports Indian enterprises developing frontier technologies that can strengthen the country's strategic technology capabilities.

On the financial front, Inc42's company database reports Astrome's FY25 revenue at over Rs 1.1 crore, although audited revenue growth and profitability figures are not publicly established in the available disclosures.
The company's funding profile lists more than $13.4 million in cumulative funding, including earlier institutional investments.

With the latest government-backed assistance, Astrome aims to accelerate the engineering and integration of its satellite constellation while expanding India's indigenous capabilities in space-based intelligence and communications.
